answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: anchored PageRank for standing. Weight an identity by its PageRank in the trust graph, but place the random-restart only on hard-to-forge anchors, not uniformly. Trust flows from anchors like light from a lantern; a vertex reachable only through other fakes gets almost none. A cluster can wire dense internal links, but anchored PageRank ignores loops no anchor feeds: rank into the cluster is bounded by its real edges to the core. A million intra-linked fakes are a million near-zero vertices, a zephyr on the wall. Gaining rank needs genuine anchor-side edges.
